steps.message: The file lives inside a `runs/` path ignored by the outer repo, so `git diff` shows nothing. Here are the actual changes:

## Summary

**Root cause**

The filter banner (`status_filter_group` → `filter_text` + "(show all)") in `GpsStatusFragment` was only ever updated from `updateFilterView()`, which is called exclusively from the satellite-status callback path (`updateGnssStatus()` / `updateLegacyStatus()`). Its visibility depended solely on whether a GNSS filter preference was set:

```java
Set<GnssType> filter = PreferenceUtils.getGnssFilter();
if (filter.isEmpty()) { filterGroup.setVisibility(View.GONE); ... }
else { filterGroup.setVisibility(View.VISIBLE); filterTextView.setText(...); }
```

When GNSS is stopped, `setStarted(false)` runs and clears every other view (lat/lon, TTFF, altitude, num sats, DOP, satellite lists), but it never touched the filter group. Since no further status callbacks arrive after stopping, `updateFilterView()` is never invoked again, so the stale "Showing 9 of 15 satellites (show all)" line stayed on screen — and `mNumSats` remained in its italic typeface.

**Fix** (`GPSTest/src/main/java/com/android/gpstest/GpsStatusFragment.java`)

1. Extracted the hide/reset logic into a new `hideFilterView()` helper that sets `filterGroup` to `GONE`, clears `filterTextView`'s text, and restores `mNumSats` to a normal (non-italic) typeface. It null-guards the views so it is safe to call before/after the view hierarchy exists.
2. Called `hideFilterView()` from `setStarted(false)`, alongside the other view resets, so stopping GNSS clears the filter text.
3. Hardened `updateFilterView()` with `if (filter.isEmpty() || !mNavigating)` so the banner can never be (re)shown while GNSS is not running, and routed its GONE branch through the same helper.

**Behavior preserved:** when GNSS restarts, `updateGnssStatus()`/`updateLegacyStatus()` call `setStarted(true)` before `updateFilterView()`, so `mNavigating` is `true` and an active filter re-displays the banner with fresh counts as before. Clearing the filter while running still hides it via the unchanged `filter.isEmpty()` branch.

**Verification:** `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` (both `google` and `osmdroid` debug flavors assembled).
